stem.en: Kabir asks how the ribosome "knows which bead comes next". What does it actually check?

text.en: Only that the tRNA's anticodon pairs with the codon in the right-hand slot. It never looks at the bead. Whatever the charging enzyme put on the hook is what goes on the chain.
It reads the codon and picks the bead.

feedback.en: The ribosome has no table. The table is in the charging enzymes. The ribosome checks three letters against three.
The bead is far from the checking site. The ribosome would join a wrong bead on a correctly paired tRNA without noticing.

text.en: It does not check anything; it joins whatever arrives.

feedback.en: A tRNA whose anticodon does not pair is rejected before joining. The check is on the pairing, and it is strict.

explanation.en: Two checks in the whole system. Charging enzymes check bead against tRNA. The ribosome checks tRNA against codon. Neither checks bead against codon, which is the sabotage lesson.
